Only they did not have this seal. You have therefore also the explanation of these. I have, I say, Lord. Now therefore, Lord, about the mountains make clear to me. Why are the appearances different and different and varied? Listen, he says. These twelve mountains are tribes that dwell in the whole world. So the Son of God was preached to them through the apostles. Why are the mountains varied and of different and different appearance, make clear to me, Lord. Listen, he says. These twelve tribes that dwell in the whole world are twelve nations. They are varied in mind and in understanding. As therefore you saw the mountains varied, such are also the varieties of the mind of the nations and the understanding. I will make clear to you also the action of each one. First, I say, Lord, make this clear, why the mountains being so varied, when their stones were placed into the building, became of one color bright, as also the stones that had come up out of the deep? Because, he says, all the nations that dwell under heaven, having heard and believed, were called upon the name of the Son of God. Having received therefore the seal, they had one mind and one understanding, and one faith of them came to be and one love, and they bore the spirits of the virgins with the name. For this reason the building of the tower became of one color bright as the sun. But after they entered into the same place and became one body, some of them defiled themselves and were cast out from the race of the righteous and became again such as they were before, but rather also worse. How, I say, Lord, did they become worse, having known God? The one who does not know, he says, God and does evil has some punishment of his evil. But the one who has known God no longer ought to do evil, but to do good. If therefore the one who ought to do good does evil, does he not seem to do more evil than the one who does not know God? For this reason those who have not known God and do evil are judged to death. But those who have known God and have seen his great works and do evil will be punished doubly and will die forever. So therefore the church of God will be cleansed. As you saw the stones taken from the tower and handed over to the evil spirits and cast out from there: and there will be one body of those who have been cleansed, just as also the tower became as if made from one stone after it was cleansed. So also will be the church of God after it is cleansed and the evil ones are cast out and hypocrites and blasphemers and the double-minded and those who do evil with various evils. After these are cast out, the church of God will be one body, one mind, one understanding, one faith, one love. And then the Son of God will rejoice and be glad in them, having received back his people pure. Greatly, I say, Lord, and gloriously all things are. Still, I say, Lord, of the mountains each one make clear to me the power and the actions, in order that every soul that trusts in the Lord, having heard, may glorify his great and wonderful and glorious name. Listen, he says, to the variety of the mountains and of the twelve nations. From the first mountain, the black one, those who believed are such: apostates and blasphemers against the Lord and traitors of the servants of God. For these repentance is not, but death is, and for this reason they are also black. For their race is lawless. From the second mountain, the bare one, those who believed are such: hypocrites and teachers of evil. These therefore are like the former ones, not having fruit of righteousness. For as their mountain is fruitless, so also such men have a name, but from the faith they are empty and there is no fruit of truth in them. For these therefore repentance is set, if they repent quickly. But if they delay, with the former ones will be their death.
Why, I say, lord, is there repentance for these, but for the first ones there is not? For their deeds are almost the same. For this reason, he says, repentance is set for these, because they did not blaspheme their Lord nor became betrayers of the servants of God; but because of desire for gain they played the hypocrite and each one taught according to the desires of the people who sin. But they will pay some penalty; yet repentance is set for them because they did not become blasphemers nor betrayers. From the third mountain, the one having thorns and thistles, those who believed are like this. Of them, some are rich, and others are entangled in many business affairs. The thistles are the rich, and the thorns are those entangled in varied business affairs. These, then, those entangled in many and varied business affairs, do not cling to the servants of God, but wander astray, being choked by their own affairs; but the rich cling to the servants of God with difficulty, fearing lest they be asked for something by them; such people, then, will enter into the kingdom of God with difficulty. For just as walking with bare feet among thistles is difficult, so also for such people it is difficult to enter into the kingdom of God. But for all these there is repentance, but a quick one, so that what they did not accomplish in former times they may now make up in the days and do something good. If, then, they repent and do something good, they will live to God; but if they remain in their deeds, they will be handed over to those women, who will put them to death. From the fourth mountain, the one having many plants, the parts above the plants green, but the parts near the roots dry, and some also being dried by the sun, those who believed are like this: some are double-minded, and others have the Lord on their lips but do not have him on their heart. For this reason their foundations are dry and have no power, and their words alone live, but their works are dead. Such people neither live nor have died. They are, then, like the double-minded; for the double-minded also are neither green nor dry; for they neither live nor have died. For just as these plants, when they saw the sun, were dried up, so also the double-minded, when they hear of tribulation, because of their cowardice commit idolatry and are ashamed of the name of their Lord. Such people, then, neither live nor have died. But these also, if they repent quickly, will be able to live; but if they do not repent, they are already handed over to the women who carry away their life. From the fifth mountain, the one having green plants and being rough, those who believed are like this: faithful indeed, but slow to learn and self-willed and pleasing themselves, wanting to know everything, and they know nothing at all. Because of this self-will of theirs, understanding departed from them, and foolish folly entered into them. They praise themselves as having understanding and want to be self-appointed teachers, being fools. Because of this arrogance, then, many were emptied while exalting themselves; for a great demon is self-will and empty confidence; from these, then, many were cast away, but some repented and believed and submitted themselves to those who have understanding, having recognized their own folly. And for the rest of such people repentance is set; for they did not become wicked, but rather foolish and without understanding. These, then, if they repent, will live to God; but if they do not repent, they will dwell with the women who do evil to them. Those from the sixth mountain, the one having great and small cracks and in the cracks withered plants, those who believed are like this. Those having the small cracks, these are those who have something against one another, and from their own slanders they are withered in faith; but many repented from these things. And the rest also will repent, when they hear my commandments; for their slanders are small, and they will repent quickly. But those having great cracks, these are persistent in their slanders and become resentful, being angry with one another; these, then, were thrown away from the tower and were rejected from its building. Such people, then, will live with difficulty. If God and our Lord, who rules over all things and has authority over all his creation, does not bear a grudge against those who confess their sins, but becomes merciful, does a man, being corruptible and full of sins, bear a grudge against a man, as though he were able to destroy or save him? But I say to you, the angel of repentance: as many of you as have this disposition, put it away and repent, and the Lord will heal your former sins, if you cleanse yourselves from this demon; but if not, you will be handed over to it unto death. From the seventh mountain, on which were green and cheerful plants, and the whole mountain flourishing, and every kind of cattle and the birds of heaven were feeding on the plants on this mountain, and the plants on which they fed became more flourishing, those who believed are like this. They were always simple and innocent and blessed, having nothing against one another, but always rejoicing over the servants of God and clothed with the Holy Spirit of these virgins and always having compassion on every person, and from their labors they supplied every person without reproach and without hesitation. The Lord, then, seeing their simplicity and all their childlikeness, multiplied them in the labors of their hands and gave them grace in all their work. But I say to you who are such, I the angel of repentance: remain such, and your seed will not be blotted out forever; for the Lord tested you and wrote you into our number, and all your seed will dwell with the Son of God; for you received from his Spirit. From the eighth mountain, where were the many springs and all the creation of the Lord was watered from the springs, those who believed are like this:
Apostles and teachers who preached into the whole world and who taught reverently and purely the word of the Lord and in no way at all embezzled for evil desire, but always in righteousness and truth walked, just as also they received the Holy Spirit. Of such ones therefore the passing is with the angels. And from the ninth mountain, the desolate one, the one having the reptiles and wild beasts in it, the ones destroying people, those who believed are like this: the ones having the spots are deacons who served badly and plundered the life of widows and orphans and gained for themselves from the ministry which they received to serve. If therefore they remain in the same desire, they died and there is no hope of life for them. But if they turn and purely complete their ministry, they will be able to live. And the ones withered, these are the ones who denied and did not turn to their Lord, but became barren and became desolate. Not clinging to the servants of God, but living alone they destroy their own souls. For as a vine left in some hedge, receiving neglect, is destroyed and by the weeds is made desolate and in time becomes wild, and no longer is useful to its master, so also such people have given up on themselves and become useless to their Lord, having become wild. For these therefore repentance happens, if they are not found to have denied from the heart. But if someone is found to have denied from the heart, I do not know if he can live. And this I do not say for these days, so that someone who denies may receive repentance. For it is impossible for the one about to deny his Lord now to be saved. But for those who denied long ago repentance seems to be laid down. If therefore someone is about to repent, let him become quick before the tower is completed. But if not, he will be destroyed by the women unto death. And the stunted ones, these are deceitful and slanderers. And the wild beasts which you saw on the mountain, these are they. For just as the wild beasts destroy a person with their own poison and destroy him, so also the words of such people destroy a person and destroy him. These therefore are stunted from their faith because of the practice which they have in themselves. But some repented and were saved. And the rest who are such can be saved, if they repent. But if they do not repent, from those women, whose power they have, they will die. And from the tenth mountain, where there were trees sheltering some sheep, those who believed are like this: bishops and hospitable ones, who gladly into their own houses always received the servants of God without hypocrisy. And the bishops always the needy and the widows with their ministry unceasingly sheltered and purely conducted themselves always. These therefore all will be sheltered by the Lord continually. Those therefore who have done these things are glorious before God and already their place is with the angels, if they remain until the end ministering to the Lord. And from the eleventh mountain, where there were trees full of fruits, adorned with different and different fruits, those who believed are like this: the ones who suffered for the name of the Son of God, who also eagerly suffered from the whole heart, and handed over their souls. Why therefore, I say, Lord, do all the trees have fruits, but some of their fruits are more beautiful? Hear, he says: as many as ever suffered for the name, are glorious before God, and the sins of all were taken away, because they suffered for the name of the Son of God. But why their fruits are varied, and some surpassing, hear. As many as, he says, brought before authority were examined and did not deny, but suffered eagerly, these are more glorious before the Lord. Of these the fruit is the surpassing one. But as many as were cowardly and in wavering and reasoned in their hearts whether they will deny or confess, and suffered, of these the fruits are lesser, because this counsel went up upon their heart. For evil is this counsel, that a servant should deny his own master. Watch therefore you who deliberate these things, lest ever this counsel remain in your hearts and you die to God. But you who suffer for the sake of the name ought to glorify God, because God considered you worthy, so that you may bear this name and all your sins may be healed. Therefore count yourselves blessed. But do not think you have done a great work, if someone of you suffers for God. Life the Lord grants you, and you do not understand. For your sins weighed you down, and if you had not suffered for the sake of the name of the Lord, because of your sins you would have died to God. These things I say to you who waver about denial or confession. Confess that you have a Lord, lest ever denying you be handed over to prison. If the nations punish their own servants, if someone denies his own lord, what do you think the Lord will do to you, who has authority over all? Lift these counsels from your hearts, so that continually you may live to God. And from the twelfth mountain, the white one, those who believed are like this: they are as infant babies, to whom no evil goes up upon the heart, nor did they know what wickedness is, but always in infancy they remained. Such ones therefore without wavering will dwell in the kingdom of God, because in no matter they defiled the commandments of God, but with infancy they remained all the days of their life in the same mind. As many therefore as will remain, he says, and will be as the babies, not having evil, more glorious than all the previously mentioned you will be. For all the babies are glorious before God and first with him. Blessed therefore are you, as many as lift from yourselves wickedness and put on innocence. First of all you will live to God.
After he finished the parables of the mountains, I say to him: Lord, now make clear to me about the stones that were taken from the plain and placed into the building in place of the stones that were taken from the tower, and about the round stones that were placed into the building, and about those still being round. Hear, he says, also about all these things. The stones taken from the plain and placed into the building of the tower in place of the rejected ones, they are the roots of the white mountain. Since therefore those who believed, from the white mountain all were found innocent, the lord of the tower commanded these to be thrown from the roots of this mountain into the building of the tower: for he knew that, if these stones go away into the building of the tower, they will remain bright and none of them will turn black. But if he had added from the other mountains, he would have had to visit that tower again and purge it. But all these were found white, those who believed and those who are about to believe: for they are from the same race. Blessed is this race, because it is innocent. Hear now also about the round and bright stones. They too are all from the white mountain. Hear, however, why they were found round. Their riches darkened them a little from the truth and clouded them, but they never withdrew from God, nor did any evil word proceed from their mouth, but all fairness and virtue of truth. Therefore when the lord had seen their mind, that they could favor the truth, and also remain good, he ordered their wealth to be cut back, for it not to be taken away from them entirely, so that they might be able to do some good from what was left to them, and they will live to God, since they are from a good race. Therefore for this reason they were cut back a little and were placed into the structure of this tower. But the rest, who still remained round and were not fitted into that structure, because they have not yet received the seal, were put back in their place; for they were found very round. But this world must be cut away from them, and the vanities of their wealth, and then they will come together into the kingdom of God. For it is necessary for them to enter into the kingdom of God; for the lord blessed this innocent race. Therefore from this race no one will perish. For even if one of them, tempted by the most wicked devil, commits some sin, he will quickly run back to his lord. I judge you all happy, I the angel of repentance, all you who are innocent like infants, because your portion is good and honored before God. But I say to all of you, all you who have received this seal, to have simplicity and not to be mindful of offenses nor to remain in your wickedness or in the memory of bitter offenses, to become one spirit each and to remove these evil divisions from among you, so that the lord of the sheep may rejoice over them. And he will rejoice, if all are found healthy, and none of them have fallen away. But if any of them are found fallen away, woe to the shepherds it will be. But if the shepherds themselves are found fallen away, what will they say to the master of the flock? That they fell away because of the sheep? They will not be believed: for it is an unbelievable thing that a shepherd should suffer anything from sheep: rather they will be punished for their lie. And I myself am a shepherd, and I must most strictly give an account for you. Therefore heal yourselves, while the tower is still being built. The Lord dwells in men who love peace; for to him peace is dear; but from the quarrelsome and those ruined by wickedness he is far away. Therefore give back to him the spirit whole, as you received it. For if you give a fuller a new garment, whole, and you wish to receive it back whole, but the fuller returns it to you torn, will you receive it? Will you not immediately become angry and pursue him with abuse, saying: I gave you a whole garment; why did you tear it and make it useless? And because of the tear that you made in it, it cannot be in use. Will you not say all these words to the fuller about the tear that he made in your garment? If therefore you grieve thus over your garment and complain that you do not receive it back whole, what do you think the Lord will do to you, who gave you a whole spirit, and you made it entirely useless, so that it can be of no use to its lord? For its use began to be useless, when it was corrupted by you. Therefore will not the lord of the spirit put you to death because of this deed of yours? Certainly, I said, all those whom he finds remaining in the memory of offenses, he will put to death. Do not trample, he said, on his mercy, but rather honor him, because he is so patient toward your sins and is not like you. Therefore do repentance that is useful to you. All these things that are written above, I the shepherd, the angel of repentance, showed and spoke to the servants of God. If therefore you believe and hear my words and walk in them and correct your ways, you will be able to live. But if you remain in wickedness and the memory of offenses, no one of this kind will live to God. All these things that had to be said by me have been said to you. The shepherd himself said to me: Have you asked me everything? And I said: Yes, lord. Why then did you not ask me about the shape of the stones put back in the structure, that we filled in the shapes? And I said: I forgot, lord. Hear now, he said, about them. These are those who have now heard my commandments and have done repentance from their whole hearts. And when the lord had seen that their repentance was good and pure and that they could remain in it, he ordered their former sins to be wiped out. For these shapes were their sins, and they were leveled, so that they might not appear.

pass_b_english: After I had written down the commandments and parables of the Shepherd, the angel of repentance, he came to me. “I want to show you,” he said, “all that the Holy Spirit showed you, the Spirit that spoke with you in the form of the Church. For that Spirit is the Son of God.

“You were too weak in the flesh, and so it was not made clear to you through an angel. But when you were given power through the Spirit and grew strong in your strength, so that you could see even an angel, then the building of the tower was revealed to you through the Church. You saw everything well and reverently, as shown by a virgin. Now you see it shown by an angel, though through the same Spirit.

“But you must learn everything more exactly from me. This is why the glorious angel gave me to dwell in your house: so that you might see everything with strength, and not be afraid of anything as you were before.”

And he led me away to Arcadia, to a rounded mountain. He sat me down on the top of the mountain and showed me a great plain. Around the plain were twelve mountains, and each mountain was different in appearance.
The first was black as soot. The second was bare, with no plants on it. The third was full of thorns and thistles.
The fourth had plants that were half dry. The tops of the plants were green, but the parts near the roots were dry. And some of the plants dried up whenever the sun scorched them.

The fifth mountain had green plants, and it was rough. The sixth mountain was full of cracks all over, some small and some large. There were plants in the cracks, but the plants were not very flourishing. They looked more as if they had withered.

The seventh mountain had cheerful plants, and the whole mountain was thriving. Every kind of cattle and bird fed on that mountain, and the more the cattle and the birds fed, the more and more the plants of that mountain flourished. The eighth mountain was full of springs, and every kind of the Lord’s creatures drank from the springs of that mountain.

The ninth mountain had no water at all and was desolate throughout. On it were wild beasts and deadly reptiles that destroy people. The tenth mountain had very great trees and was all in shade, and under the shelter of the trees sheep lay resting and chewing the cud.

The eleventh mountain was very thick with trees, and those trees were laden with fruit. They were adorned with fruit of one kind and another, so that anyone who saw them would long to eat of their fruit. The twelfth mountain was all white, and its look was cheerful. The mountain in itself was most beautiful.
In the middle of the plain he showed me a great white rock that had risen up out of the plain. The rock was higher than the mountains, and square, so that it could hold the whole world.
That rock was old, and a gate had been cut out of it. But the carving of the gate seemed to me to be recent. The gate shone so much brighter than the sun that I marveled at the radiance of the gate.

Around the gate stood twelve virgins. The four who stood at the corners seemed to me the more glorious, but the others were glorious too. They stood at the four sides of the gate, and between them stood the others, two by two.
They wore linen tunics and were beautifully girded, with their right shoulders bare, as if they were about to carry some load. That is how ready they were, for they were very cheerful and eager.

When I had seen these things, I marveled within myself, because I was seeing great and glorious things. And then I was perplexed about the virgins. Delicate as they were, they stood bravely, as if they were about to carry the whole of heaven.

And the Shepherd said to me, “Why are you reasoning within yourself, and perplexed, and bringing grief on yourself? Whatever you cannot grasp, do not attempt, if you are a man of understanding. Ask the Lord instead, so that you may receive understanding and grasp these things.

“You cannot see what is behind you, but you do see what is in front of you. So let alone what you cannot see, and do not torture yourself. But what you do see, make yourself master of that, and do not pry into the rest. I will make clear to you everything that I show you. So look now at what remains.”

I saw that six men had come, tall and glorious and alike in appearance, and they called a multitude of men. Those who came were tall men too, handsome and strong. The six men ordered them to build a tower upon the rock. And there was a great commotion among those men who had come to build the tower, as they ran here and there around the gate.

The virgins standing around the gate kept telling the men to hurry on with the building of the tower. And the virgins had stretched out their hands, as if they were about to receive something from the men.
Then the six men ordered stones to come up from a certain deep place and go into the building of the tower. And ten stones came up, square and bright, and not hewn.

The six men called the virgins and ordered them to carry all the stones that were to go into the building of the tower. The virgins were to pass through the gate with the stones and hand them to the men who were to build the tower.
The virgins loaded one another with the first ten stones, the ones that had come up from the deep, and together they carried them, one stone at a time.

Just as they had stood together around the gate, so they carried. Those who seemed to be strong had gone in under the corners of the stone, and the others had gone in under its sides. In this way they carried all the stones. They brought them through the gate, as they had been ordered, and handed them to the men for the tower. And the men took the stones and built.

The tower was built upon the great rock and above the gate. Those ten stones were fitted together, and they filled the whole rock. They became the foundation of the building of the tower. And the rock and the gate carried the whole tower.

After the ten stones, another twenty stones came up from the deep. These too were fitted into the building of the tower, carried by the virgins just as the first ones had been. After these, thirty-five came up, and these were fitted into the tower in the same way. After these, another forty stones came up, and all of them were put into the building of the tower. So there were four courses in the foundations of the tower.

Then the stones stopped coming up from the deep, and the builders also stopped for a little while. And the six men again commanded the great crowd to bring stones from the mountains for the building of the tower.

So stones of many colors were brought from all the mountains, hewn by the men, and they were handed to the virgins. The virgins carried them through the gate and handed them in for the building of the tower. And when the stones of many colors were set in the building, they all alike became white, and they changed their many colors.

But some stones were handed in for the building by the men, and these did not become bright. As they were when they were set there, so they were found. For they had not been handed in by the virgins, and they had not been carried through the gate. So these stones were unsightly in the building of the tower.
When the six men saw the unsightly stones in the building, they ordered them to be taken out and carried back down to their own place, the place they had been brought from.

And they said to the men who were bringing in the stones, “You are not to hand in any stones for the building at all. Set them down beside the tower, so that the virgins may carry them through the gate and hand them in for the building. For if they are not carried through the gate by the hands of these virgins, they cannot change their colors. So do not labor in vain.”

On that day the building came to an end, but the tower was not completed, for it was to be built up further. So there was a pause in the building. The six men ordered all the builders to withdraw for a little while and rest. But they commanded the virgins not to withdraw from the tower. It seemed to me that the virgins had been left behind to guard the tower.

When they had all withdrawn and were at rest, I said to the Shepherd, “Sir, why was the building of the tower not finished?” He said, “The tower cannot be completed yet, not until its lord comes and tests this building, so that if any stones are found to be rotten, he may change them. For the tower is being built according to his will.”

“Sir,” I said, “I would like to know what this building of the tower is, and about the rock and the gate, the mountains and the virgins. I would like to know about the stones that came up from the deep and were not hewn, but went into the building just as they were. And why were ten stones laid first in the foundations, then twenty, then thirty-five, then forty? And what of the stones that went into the building and were taken out again and put back in their own place? Set my soul at rest about all these things, sir, and make them known to me.”

He said, “If your eagerness is not found to be empty, you will know everything. For after a few days we will come here, and you will see the rest of what is to come upon this tower, and you will know all the parables exactly.”

After a few days we came to the place where we had sat. He said to me, “Let us go to the tower, for the owner of the tower is coming to inspect it.” So we came to the tower, and there was no one beside it at all, only the virgins.
The Shepherd asked the virgins whether the master of the tower had arrived. They said that he was about to come and inspect the building.
And look, after a little while I saw an array of many men coming. In the middle was a man so tall that he rose higher than the tower.

The six men who were in charge of the building walked with him on his right and on his left. All those who had worked on the building were with him, and around him were many other glorious ones. The virgins who were keeping watch over the tower ran up and kissed him, and they began to walk near him around the tower.
That man inspected the building closely, so closely that he felt each stone, one by one. He held a rod in his hand, and he struck every single stone that had been built in.

And when he struck them, some of them turned black as soot. Some turned scabby, some had cracks, some were stunted, some were neither white nor black, some were rough and did not fit with the other stones, and some had many spots. These were the different kinds of rotten stones that were found in the building.
So he ordered all of these to be taken out of the tower and set down beside the tower, and other stones to be brought and put in their place.

The builders asked him from which mountain he wanted stones to be brought and put in their place. He did not order them to be brought from the mountains. He ordered them to be brought from a plain that lay nearby.
So the plain was dug, and bright stones were found, square ones, and some round ones too. Every stone that was in that plain was brought, and the virgins carried them through the gate.

The square stones were hewn and set in the place of those that had been taken out. But the round ones were not set in the building, because they were hard to hew and the hewing went slowly. They were set down beside the tower, since they were going to be hewn and set in the building, for they were very bright.

When the glorious man, the lord of the whole tower, had finished these things, he called the Shepherd to him. He handed over to him all the stones that lay beside the tower, the ones that had been cast out of the building, and he said to him,
“Clean these stones carefully, and set in the building of the tower those that can fit with the rest. But those that do not fit, throw far away from the tower.”
When he had given the Shepherd these orders, he went away from the tower with all those who had come with him. But the virgins stood around the tower, keeping watch over it.

I said to the Shepherd, “How can these stones go into the building of the tower, when they have been rejected?” He answered me, “Do you see these stones?” “I see them, sir,” I said. He said, “I myself will hew the greater part of these stones and put them into the building, and they will fit with the rest of the stones.”

“Sir,” I said, “how can they fill the same space once they have been cut down?” He answered me, “Those that are found to be small will be put in the middle of the building. Those that are larger will be set on the outside, and they will hold the small ones together.”

After saying this to me, he went on, “Let us go. After two days let us come and clean these stones and put them into the building. For everything around the tower must be cleaned. Otherwise the master may come suddenly and find the place around the tower dirty, and be angry. Then these stones will not go into the building of the tower, and I will seem careless in the master’s eyes.”
After two days we came to the tower, and he said to me, “Let us inspect all the stones and see which ones can go into the building.” I said to him, “Sir, let us inspect them.”

We began with the black stones and inspected them first. As they were when they were put out of the building, so they were found. And the Shepherd ordered them to be carried away from the tower and set apart.

Next he inspected the scabby stones. He took many of them and hewed them, and he ordered the virgins to take them up and put them into the building. The virgins took them up and set them in the middle of the building of the tower. The rest he ordered to be put with the black stones, for these too were found to be black.

Next he inspected the stones that had cracks. He hewed many of these too, and he ordered that the virgins carry them away into the building. They were set on the outside, because they were found to be sounder. The rest could not be hewn, because their cracks were so many. For this reason they were cast out from the building of the tower.

Next he inspected the stunted stones. Many among them were found to be black, and some had developed great cracks. He ordered these too to be put with the stones that had been cast out. But the ones left over he cleaned and hewed, and he ordered them to be set in the building. The virgins took them up and fitted them into the middle of the building of the tower, for they were weaker.

Next he inspected the stones that were half white and half black. Many of them were found to be black, and he ordered these too to be taken away with the stones that had been cast out. All the rest were taken up by the virgins. Because they were white, the virgins themselves fitted them into the building. They were set on the outside, because they were found to be sound, so that they could hold the stones set in the middle. For nothing at all had been cut away from them.

Next he inspected the rough, hard stones. A few of them were cast out because they could not be hewn, for they were found to be very hard. The rest of them were hewn, and the virgins took them up and fitted them into the middle of the building of the tower, for they were weaker.

Next he inspected the stones that had the spots. A very few of these had turned black, and they were cast out with the others. Those left over were found to be bright and sound, and the virgins fitted these too into the building. They were set on the outside because of their strength.
Then he came to inspect the white, round stones, and he said to me, “What are we to do about these stones?” “Sir,” I said, “what do I know?” He said, “So you have no thought about them at all?”

“Sir,” I said, “I do not have this craft. I am not a stonecutter, and I cannot work it out.” He said, “Do you not see that they are very round? If I want to make them square, a great deal must be cut away from them. Yet some of them must of necessity be set in the building.”

“Sir,” I said, “if it is a necessity, why do you torment yourself? Why not choose the ones you want for the building and fit them into it?” He chose the larger, bright ones from among them and hewed them, and the virgins took them up and fitted them into the outer parts of the building.

The rest, those left over, were taken up and put back in the plain they had been brought from. But they were not cast out. “For,” said the Shepherd, “a little of the tower still remains to be built. And the master of the tower wants all these stones to be fitted into the building, because they are very bright.”

Then twelve women were called. They were very lovely in appearance. They were dressed in black and girded, with their shoulders bare and their hair hanging loose. These women seemed to me to be wild. The Shepherd ordered them to take up the stones that had been cast out of the building and carry them away to the mountains they had been brought from.

Cheerfully the women took up all the stones, carried them away, and set them down where they had been taken from. When all the stones had been taken up and not a stone lay around the tower any longer, the Shepherd said to me, “Let us go around the tower and see whether there is any defect in it.” So I went around it with him.

When the Shepherd saw that the tower was beautiful in its building, he was very cheerful. For the tower was built in such a way that when I saw it, I longed for its building. It was built as if from a single stone, with not one joint in it. The stone looked as if it had been carved out of the rock, for it seemed to me to be all one stone.

I too was cheerful as I walked with him and saw such good things. Then the Shepherd said to me, “Go and bring lime and finely crushed pottery, so that I may fill up the hollows left by the stones that were taken up and put into the building. For everything around the tower must be made level.”

I did as he ordered and brought them to him. “Assist me,” he said, “and the work will soon be finished.” So he filled up the hollows left by the stones that had gone into the building, and he ordered the place around the tower to be swept and made clean.
The virgins took brooms and swept. They cleared all the filth away from the tower and sprinkled water, and the place of the tower became cheerful and most beautiful.
The Shepherd said to me, “Everything has been cleaned. If the lord comes to visit the tower, he has nothing to blame us for.” When he had said this, he wanted to go.

But I caught hold of his bag and began to adjure him by the Lord to explain to me what he had shown me. He said to me, “I am busy for a little while, and then I will explain everything to you. Wait for me here until I come.”

I said to him, “Sir, what am I to do here all alone?” “You are not alone,” he said, “for these virgins are with you.” “Then hand me over to them,” I said. The Shepherd called them to him and said to them, “I entrust this man to you until I come.” And he went away.
So I was alone with the virgins. They were all the more cheerful, and they were kind to me, above all the four who were the more glorious among them.

The virgins said to me, “The Shepherd is not coming here today.” “Then what am I to do?” I said. They said, “Wait for him until evening. If he comes, he will speak with you. But if he does not come, you will stay here with us until he does.”

I said to them, “I will wait for him until evening. But if he does not come, I will go home and come back in the morning.” But they answered me, “You were handed over to us. You cannot go away from us.”

“Then where am I to stay?” I said. They said, “You will sleep with us as a brother, and not as a husband. For you are our brother, and from now on we are going to dwell with you, for we love you very much.” But I was ashamed to stay with them.
Then the one who seemed to be first among them began to kiss me and embrace me. When the others saw her embracing me, they too began to kiss me, and to lead me around the tower, and to play with me.

And it was as if I had become a younger man, and I too began to play with them. For some of them were dancing in a ring, others were leaping in dance, and others were singing. But I kept silent and walked with them around the tower, and I was cheerful with them.
When evening came, I wanted to go home. But they would not let me go. They held me back. So I stayed the night with them, and I slept beside the tower.

For the virgins spread their linen tunics on the ground and made me lie down in the middle of them, and they did nothing at all but pray. And I prayed with them without ceasing, no less than they did. The virgins rejoiced that I was praying in this way. And I stayed there with the virgins until the next day, until the second hour.

Then the Shepherd arrived, and he said to the virgins, “You have not mistreated him in any way, have you?” “Ask him,” they said. I said to him, “Sir, I was glad to stay with them.” “What did you dine on?” he asked. “Sir,” I said, “I dined on the words of the Lord the whole night long.” “Did they receive you well?” he asked. “Yes, sir,” I said.

“Now,” said the Shepherd, “what do you want to hear first?” “Just as you showed it to me from the beginning, sir,” I said. “I ask you, sir, to make each thing clear to me as I question you.” “As you wish,” he said. “That is how I will explain it to you, and I will hide nothing at all from you.”

“First of all, sir,” I said, “make this clear to me. The rock and the gate: what are they?” “This rock and the gate are the Son of God,” he said. “Sir,” I said, “how is it that the rock is old, but the gate is new?” “Listen,” he said, “and understand, you who lack understanding.
“The Son of God is older than all his creation, so that he was the Father’s counselor in his creation. That is why the rock is old.” “But the gate, sir,” I said, “why is it new?”
“Because he was revealed in the last days, the days of the end,” he said. “That is why the gate was made new, so that those who are going to be saved may enter the kingdom of God through it.

“Did you see,” he said, “how the stones that came in through the gate were put into the building of the tower, while those that did not come in through it were cast back out to their own place?” “I saw it, sir,” I said. “In the same way,” he said, “no one will enter the kingdom of God unless he receives his holy name.

“For if you want to enter a certain city, and that city has a wall all around it and one gate, can you enter that city except through the gate it has?” “How could it be any other way, sir?” I said. “Then if you cannot enter the city except through the gate it has,” he said, “so too a person cannot enter the kingdom of God in any other way than through the name of his Son, whom he loves.

“Did you see the crowd that was building the tower?” he said. “I saw them, sir,” I said. “They are all glorious angels,” he said. “The Lord is walled around by them. But the gate is the Son of God. This is the one way in to the Lord. So no one will come in to him in any other way than through his Son.
“Did you see the six men,” he said, “and the glorious and great man in the middle of them, who walked around the tower and rejected the stones from the building?” “I saw them, sir,” I said.

“The glorious man is the Son of God,” he said, “and those six are the glorious angels who support him on the right and on the left. Not one of these glorious angels,” he said, “will come in to God without him. Whoever does not receive his name will not enter the kingdom of God.”
“And the tower,” I said, “what is it?” “This tower is the church,” he said.

“And these virgins, who are they?” I asked. “They are holy spirits,” he said, “and a person cannot be found in the kingdom of God unless these virgins clothe him with their garment. For if you receive the name alone, and do not receive the garment from them, it will do you no good. For these virgins are powers of the Son of God. If you wear the name but do not wear his power, you will be wearing his name in vain.

“As for the stones you saw cast out,” he said, “they wore the name, but they did not put on the clothing of the virgins.” “What kind of clothing do they have, sir?” I asked. “Their very names are their clothing,” he said. “Whoever wears the name of the Son of God ought to wear their names as well. For even the Son himself wears the names of these virgins.
“All the stones that you saw go into the building of the tower,” he said, “handed in by the virgins’ hands and remaining in the building, are clothed with the power of these virgins.

“That is why you see that the tower has become a single stone with the rock. So too those who have believed in the Lord through his Son, and are clothed with these spirits, will become one spirit and one body, and their clothes will be of one color. And those who wear the names of the virgins, people such as these, have their dwelling in the tower.”

“Then the stones that were cast out, sir,” I said, “why were they cast out? For they passed through the gate, and they were set in the building of the tower by the hands of the virgins.” “Since you care about everything,” he said, “and inquire so closely, hear about the stones that were cast out.

“They all received the name of the Son of God,” he said, “and they received the power of these virgins as well. So when they received these spirits, they were made strong, and they were with the servants of God. They had one spirit and one body and one garment, for they were of the same mind, and they practiced righteousness.

“Then, after a time, they were won over by the women you saw dressed in black, with their shoulders bare and their hair hanging loose, beautiful women. When they saw them, they desired them and put on their power, and they took off the garment and the power of the virgins.

“So they were cast out from the house of God and handed over to those women. But those who were not deceived by the beauty of these women remained in the house of God. There,” he said, “you have the explanation of those that were cast out.”

“What then, sir,” I said, “if these people, such as they are, repent? What if they cast off the desires of these women, and return to the virgins, and walk in their power and in their works? Will they not enter the house of God?”

“They will enter,” he said, “if they cast off the works of these women, and take up the power of the virgins, and walk in their works. That is the very reason there was a pause in the building: so that, if these people repent, they may go into the building of the tower. But if they do not repent, then others will go in, and these will be thrown out for good.”

For all these things I gave thanks to the Lord, because he had compassion on all who call on his name, and sent the angel of repentance to us who had sinned against him. He renewed our spirit, and when we were already ruined and had no hope of life, he made our life new.

“Now, sir,” I said, “make clear to me why the tower is not built on the ground, but on the rock and on the gate.” “Are you still foolish and without understanding?” he said. “Sir,” I said, “I have to ask you about everything, because I cannot grasp anything at all. For all these things are great and glorious, and hard for people to understand.”

“Listen,” he said. “The name of the Son of God is great, and nothing can contain it, and it carries the whole world. If, then, all creation is carried by the Son of God, what do you think of those who are called by him, who wear the name of the Son of God and walk in his commandments?

“Do you see, then, what kind of people he carries? Those who wear his name with their whole heart. So he himself has become their foundation, and he carries them gladly, because they are not ashamed to wear his name.”
“Sir,” I said, “tell me the names of the virgins, and of the women dressed in black.” “Hear the names of the stronger virgins,” he said, “the ones who stood at the corners.

“The first is Faith, the second Self-Control, the third Power, and the fourth Patience. The others, who stood between them, have these names: Simplicity, Innocence, Purity, Cheerfulness, Truth, Understanding, Harmony, Love. Whoever wears these names, and the name of the Son of God, will be able to enter the kingdom of God.

“Hear also,” he said, “the names of the women who have the black clothes. Of these, too, four are more powerful. The first is Unbelief, the second Lack of Self-Control, the third Disobedience, and the fourth Deceit. Those who follow them are called Grief, Wickedness, Licentiousness, Anger, Falsehood, Folly, Slander, Hatred. The servant of God who wears these names will see the kingdom of God, but he will not enter it.”

“And the stones, sir,” I said, “the ones from the deep that were fitted into the building, who are they?” “The first ones,” he said, “the ten that were set in the foundations, are the first generation. The twenty-five are the second generation, of righteous men. The thirty-five are prophets of God and his ministers. And the forty are apostles and teachers of the preaching of the Son of God.”
“Then why, sir,” I said, “did the virgins hand in these stones too for the building of the tower, after carrying them through the gate?”

“Because these were the first to wear these spirits,” he said, “and they never parted from one another at all, neither the spirits from the people nor the people from the spirits. The spirits stayed with them until they fell asleep. And if they had not had these spirits with them, they would not have been of use for the building of this tower.”

“Make one thing more clear to me, sir,” I said. “What more are you asking?” he said. “Why was it, sir,” I said, “that the stones came up from the deep and were set in the building of the tower, when they had worn these spirits?”
“They had to come up through water,” he said, “so that they might be made alive. For they could not enter the kingdom of God in any other way than by laying aside the deadness of their former life.

“So these too, who had fallen asleep, received the seal of the Son of God and entered the kingdom of God. For before a person wears the name of the Son of God,” he said, “he is dead. But when he receives the seal, he lays aside deadness and takes up life.

“The seal, then, is the water. They go down into the water dead, and they come up alive. So this seal was preached to them as well, and they made use of it, so that they might enter the kingdom of God.”

“Why, sir,” I said, “did the forty stones also come up from the deep with them, when they already had the seal?” “Because these apostles and teachers preached the name of the Son of God,” he said. “And when they had fallen asleep in the power and faith of the Son of God, they preached also to those who had fallen asleep before them. They themselves gave them the seal of the preaching.

“So they went down with them into the water, and came up again. But the apostles and teachers went down alive and came up alive. Those who had fallen asleep before them went down dead, but came up alive.

“Through the apostles and teachers, then, they were made alive, and came to know the name of the Son of God. That is why they also came up together with them, and were fitted together with them into the building of the tower, and were built in without being hewn. For they had fallen asleep in righteousness and in great purity. Only they did not have this seal. So you have the explanation of these things as well.” “I have it, sir,” I said.

“Now then, sir, tell me about the mountains. Why does each one look different from the next, and why are they varied?” “Listen,” he said. “These twelve mountains are the tribes that inhabit the whole world. And the Son of God was preached to them through the apostles.”

“But make clear to me, sir,” I said, “why the mountains are varied, each with a different appearance.” “Listen,” he said. “These twelve tribes that inhabit the whole world are twelve nations. And they are varied in their thinking and in their mind. As varied as the mountains you saw, so varied are the minds of these nations, and their thinking. And I will make clear to you the conduct of each one as well.”

“First, sir,” I said, “make this clear. The mountains are so varied. Why, then, when their stones were set in the building, did they become bright and of one color, like the stones that had come up from the deep?”

“Because all the nations that live under heaven,” he said, “when they heard and believed, were called by the name of the Son of God. So when they received the seal, they had one way of thinking and one mind. Their faith became one, and their love became one, and together with the name they wore the spirits of the virgins. That is why the building of the tower became one color, bright as the sun.

“But after they had come in together and become one body, some of them defiled themselves. They were thrown out of the family of the righteous, and became again what they had been before, or rather, even worse.”

“Sir,” I said, “how did they become worse, when they had come to know God?” “The one who does not know God and does evil,” he said, “has a certain punishment for his wickedness. But the one who has come to know God ought to do evil no longer. He ought to do good.

“So if the one who ought to do good does evil, does he not seem to do greater wickedness than the one who does not know God? That is why those who have not known God and do evil are condemned to death. But those who have known God and have seen his mighty works, and do evil, will be punished twice over, and they will die forever. In this way, then, the church of God will be cleansed.

“You saw how the stones were taken out of the tower, handed over to the evil spirits, and thrown out from there. And there will be one body of those who have been cleansed, just as the tower, after it was cleansed, became as though it were made of a single stone. So it will be with the church of God as well, after it has been cleansed, and the wicked have been cast out, and the hypocrites, and the blasphemers, and the double-minded, and those who do evil in all kinds of wickedness.

“After these have been cast out, the church of God will be one body, one way of thinking, one mind, one faith, one love. And then the Son of God will rejoice and be glad in them, when he has received his people back pure.”

“Sir,” I said, “all of this is great and glorious. Now make still more clear to me, sir, the power and the deeds of each one of the mountains, so that every soul that trusts in the Lord may hear, and glorify his great and wonderful and glorious name.” “Hear,” he said, “about the variety of the mountains and of the twelve nations.

“From the first mountain, the black one, those who believed are like this: apostates, and blasphemers against the Lord, and betrayers of the servants of God. For them there is no repentance, but there is death. That is why they are black, for their kind is lawless.

“From the second mountain, the bare one, those who believed are like this: hypocrites, and teachers of wickedness. These too are like the first, for they have no fruit of righteousness. Just as their mountain is without fruit, so people like this have the name, but they are empty of faith, and there is no fruit of truth in them. For these, repentance is open, if they repent quickly. But if they delay, their death will be with the first.”

“Why, sir,” I said, “is there repentance for these, but none for the first? For their deeds are almost the same.” “Repentance is open to these,” he said, “for this reason: they did not blaspheme their Lord, and they did not become betrayers of the servants of God. It was out of desire for gain that they played the hypocrite, and each one taught to suit the desires of people who were sinning. But they will pay some penalty. Yet repentance is open to them, because they did not become blasphemers or betrayers.

“From the third mountain, the one with thorns and thistles, those who believed are like this. Some of them are rich, and others are tangled up in many business affairs. The thistles are the rich, and the thorns are those who are tangled up in business of every kind.

“Those who are tangled up in many kinds of business do not hold fast to the servants of God. They wander away, choked by their own dealings. And the rich find it hard to hold fast to the servants of God, because they are afraid of being asked for something by them. So people like this will find it hard to enter the kingdom of God.
“For just as it is hard to walk among thistles with bare feet, so it is hard for people like this to enter the kingdom of God.

“But for all of these there is repentance, a swift repentance, so that now, in these days, they may make up for what they did not do in earlier times, and do some good. If, then, they repent and do some good, they will live to God. But if they persist in their deeds, they will be handed over to those women, and the women will put them to death.

“From the fourth mountain, the one with many plants, green at the top but dry near the roots, and some withered by the sun, those who believed are like this. Some are double-minded. Others have the Lord on their lips, but do not have him in their heart.

“That is why their foundations are dry and have no power. Only their words are alive, but their works are dead. People like this are neither alive nor dead. So they are like the double-minded. For the double-minded are neither green nor dry, since they are neither alive nor dead.
“For just as these plants withered when they saw the sun, so the double-minded, when they hear of tribulation, worship idols out of cowardice, and are ashamed of the name of their Lord.

“People like this, then, are neither alive nor dead. Yet these too, if they repent quickly, will be able to live. But if they do not repent, they have already been handed over to the women who carry off their life.

“From the fifth mountain, the one that has green plants and is rough, those who believed are like this. They are believers, but slow to learn, and self-willed, and pleased with themselves. They want to know everything, and they know nothing at all.

“Because of this self-will of theirs, understanding departed from them, and senseless folly entered into them. They praise themselves as though they had understanding, and they want to make themselves teachers, though they are fools.

“Because of this haughtiness, then, many have been emptied by exalting themselves. For self-will and empty confidence are a great demon. So many of these were cast out. But some repented and believed, and put themselves under those who have understanding, for they recognized their own folly.

“And for the rest who are like this, repentance is open. For they were not wicked, but rather senseless and without understanding. So if these repent, they will live to God. But if they do not repent, they will dwell with the women who do them evil.
“From the sixth mountain, the one with great and small cracks, and withered plants in the cracks, those who believed are like this.

“Those with the small cracks are the ones who hold something against one another, and their own slanders have withered them in the faith. But many of them have repented. And the rest will repent too, when they hear my commandments. For their slanders are small, and they will repent quickly.

“But those with great cracks persist in their slanders. They hold grudges and nurse their wrath against one another. So these were flung away from the tower and rejected from its building. People like this will find it hard to live.

“Our God and Lord rules over all things and has authority over all his creation. If he holds no grudge against those who confess their sins, but is merciful, does a human being, mortal and full of sins, hold a grudge against another human being, as though he were able to destroy him or to save him?

“And I, the angel of repentance, say to you: all of you who hold to this way, lay it aside and repent, and the Lord will heal your former sins, if you cleanse yourselves of this demon. But if not, you will be handed over to it for death.

“On the seventh mountain the plants were green and cheerful, and the whole mountain was thriving. Every kind of cattle, and the birds of the air, fed on the plants on this mountain, and the plants they fed on grew all the more lush. From this mountain, those who believed are like this.

“They were always simple and innocent and blessed. They held nothing against one another, but always rejoiced in the servants of God. They were clothed with the Holy Spirit of these virgins, and they always had compassion for every person. Out of their own labors they provided for every person, without reproaching anyone and without hesitating.
“So the Lord, seeing their simplicity and all their childlikeness, made them abound in the labors of their hands, and gave them favor in everything they did.

“And I, the angel of repentance, say to you who are like this: remain as you are, and your offspring will never be blotted out. For the Lord has tested you and written you into our number, and all your offspring will dwell with the Son of God. For you have received of his Spirit.
“From the eighth mountain, where the many springs were, and all the Lord’s creation drank from the springs, those who believed are like this.

“They are apostles and teachers who preached to the whole world, and who taught the word of the Lord reverently and purely. They kept nothing at all back for evil desire, but always walked in righteousness and truth, just as they had received the Holy Spirit. So the passage of such people is with the angels.
“From the ninth mountain, the desolate one, which had in it the reptiles and wild beasts that destroy people, those who believed are like this.

“Those with the spots are deacons who served badly. They plundered the livelihood of widows and orphans, and made gain for themselves out of the ministry they had received to carry out. So if they persist in the same desire, they are dead, and there is no hope of life for them. But if they turn back and fulfill their ministry in purity, they will be able to live.

“The scabby ones are those who denied and did not turn back to their Lord. They have become barren and desolate. They do not hold fast to the servants of God, but keep to themselves, and so they destroy their own souls.

“For a vine that is left inside some hedge and gets no care is ruined. The weeds make it desolate, and in time it grows wild, and it is no longer of any use to its master. In the same way, people like this have given up on themselves, and having grown wild, they become useless to their Lord.
“For these, then, there is repentance, if they are not found to have denied from the heart. But if anyone is found to have denied from the heart, I do not know whether he can live.

“And I do not say this for these present days, so that someone may deny and then receive repentance. For it is impossible for anyone to be saved who is going to deny his Lord now. But for those who denied long ago, repentance seems to be open. So if anyone is going to repent, let him be quick, before the tower is finished. Otherwise he will be destroyed by the women and brought to death.

“And the stunted ones are the deceitful and the slanderers. The wild beasts you saw on the mountain are these people too. For just as the wild beasts destroy a person with their venom and kill him, so the words of people like this destroy a person and kill him.

“So these are stunted in their faith, because of the conduct they have within them. But some have repented and been saved. And the rest who are like this can be saved, if they repent. But if they do not repent, they will die at the hands of those women, whose power they have.
“From the tenth mountain, where there were trees sheltering some sheep, those who believed are like this.

“They are bishops and hospitable people, who were always glad to welcome the servants of God into their homes, without hypocrisy. And the bishops always sheltered the needy and the widows by their ministry, without ceasing, and always lived in purity.

“So all these will be sheltered by the Lord at all times. Those who have done these things are glorious before God, and their place is already with the angels, if they continue to the end in serving the Lord.
“From the eleventh mountain, where there were trees full of fruit, adorned with fruit of one kind and another, those who believed are like this.
“They are those who suffered for the name of the Son of God. They suffered willingly, with their whole heart, and gave up their lives.”

“Then why, sir,” I said, “do all the trees have fruit, yet some of their fruits are more beautiful?” “Listen,” he said. “All who have ever suffered for the name are glorious before God, and the sins of all of them have been taken away, because they suffered for the name of the Son of God. But hear why their fruits are varied, and why some surpass the rest.

“Those who were brought before the authorities and questioned,” he said, “and did not deny, but suffered willingly, are all the more glorious before the Lord. Theirs is the fruit that surpasses. But others were cowardly and hesitated. They reasoned in their hearts whether to deny or to confess, and then they suffered. The fruits of these are lesser, because this thought arose in their heart. For it is a wicked thought, that a servant should deny his own lord.

“So take care, you who entertain such thoughts, that this thought does not remain in your hearts, and you die to God. But you who suffer for the sake of the name ought to glorify God, because God has counted you worthy to carry this name, and to have all your sins healed.

“So count yourselves blessed. Rather, consider that you have done a great work, if any of you suffers for God’s sake. The Lord is granting you life, and you do not realize it. For your sins weighed you down, and if you had not suffered for the sake of the Lord’s name, you would have died to God because of your sins.
“I say this to you who hesitate between denying and confessing. Confess that you have a Lord, or else, denying him, you will be handed over to prison.

“If the nations punish their servants when one of them denies his lord, what do you think the Lord will do to you, he who has authority over all things? Take these thoughts out of your hearts, so that you may live to God always.

“From the twelfth mountain, the white one, those who believed are like this. They are like little babies. No evil enters their heart, and they have never known what wickedness is, but have always remained childlike.

“People like this, then, will dwell in the kingdom of God without any question, because in nothing did they defile the commandments of God. They remained childlike all the days of their life, in the same way of thinking.

“So all of you who continue,” he said, “and are like babies, having no evil, will be more glorious than all those I have spoken of. For all babies are glorious before God, and they come first with him. Blessed are you, then, all who put wickedness away from yourselves and put on innocence. You will live to God before all others.”

When he had finished the parables of the mountains, I said to him, “Sir, now tell me about the stones that were taken from the plain and set in the building in place of the stones that were taken out of the tower. Tell me also about the round stones that were set in the building, and about those that are still round.”
“Hear about all these as well,” he said. “The stones that were taken from the plain and set in the building of the tower, in place of those that were cast out, are the roots of the white mountain.

“Since those who believed from the white mountain were all found innocent, the lord of the tower ordered these stones from the roots of this mountain to be put into the building of the tower. For he knew that if these stones went into the building of the tower, they would stay bright, and not one of them would turn black.

“But if he had added stones from the other mountains, he would have had to visit that tower again and cleanse it. Yet all these have been found white, those who have believed and those who are going to believe, for they are of the same kind. Blessed is this kind, because it is innocent.

“Now hear also about the round, bright stones. They too are all from the white mountain. But hear why they were found round. Their riches have clouded them a little from the truth, and darkened them. Yet they never departed from God, and no evil word came out of their mouth, but all uprightness and the virtue of truth.

“The Lord saw their mind, that they could favor the truth and also remain good. So he ordered their wealth to be cut down, yet not taken from them altogether, so that they might be able to do some good with what was left to them. And they will live to God, because they are of a good kind. That is why they were cut down a little and set in the building of this tower.

“But the rest, who have still remained round and have not been fitted into that building, because they have not yet received the seal, were put back in their place. For they were found to be very round.

“This world must be cut away from them, and the vanities of their riches, and then they will fit into the kingdom of God. For they must enter the kingdom of God, because the Lord has blessed this innocent kind. So not one of this kind will be lost. For even if one of them is tempted by the most wicked devil and does some wrong, he will quickly run back to his Lord.
“I, the angel of repentance, count you all happy, all of you who are innocent as infants, because your portion is good and honored before God.

“And I say to all of you who have received this seal: hold to simplicity, and do not keep offenses in mind. Do not remain in your malice, or in the bitter memory of offenses. Become of one spirit, every one of you, and mend these evil cracks and take them away from among you, so that the lord of the sheep may rejoice over them.
“And he will rejoice if all are found sound, and none of them have fallen away. But if some of them are found to have fallen away, woe to the shepherds.

“And if the shepherds themselves are found to have fallen away, what will they say to the master of the flock? That they fell away because of the sheep? They will not be believed. For it is past belief that a shepherd should suffer anything from his sheep. Rather, they will be punished for their lie. And I am a shepherd too, and I must most strictly give an account for you.

“So mend yourselves, while the tower is still being built. The Lord dwells in those who love peace, for peace is truly dear to him. But he is far from the quarrelsome and from those who are lost in malice. So give the spirit back to him whole, as you received it.

“For if you give a fuller a new garment, whole, and you want to get it back whole, but the fuller returns it to you torn, will you accept it? Will you not flare up at once and go after him with reproaches? You will say, ‘I gave you a whole garment. Why have you torn it and made it useless? Because of the tear you made in it, it cannot be used.’ Will you not say all these things to the fuller, then, about the tear he has made in your garment?

“If, then, you are so grieved over your garment, and complain that you did not get it back whole, what do you think the Lord will do to you? He gave you the spirit whole, and you have made it wholly useless, so that it can be of no use at all to its Lord. For its use became useless when it was spoiled by you. Will not the Lord of that spirit, then, punish you with death for this deed of yours?”
“Certainly,” I said. “He will so punish all those he finds holding on to the memory of offenses.”
“Do not trample on his mercy,” he said. “Honor him instead, because he is so patient with your offenses, and is not like you. So repent, with a repentance that is of use to you.

“All these things that are written above, I, the Shepherd, the angel of repentance, have shown and spoken to the servants of God. So if you believe, and hear my words, and walk in them, and set your ways right, you will be able to live. But if you remain in malice and in the memory of offenses, no one of that kind will live to God. All these things that I was to say have now been said to you.”

The Shepherd himself said to me, “Have you asked me everything?” And I said, “Yes, sir.” “Then why,” he said, “have you not asked me about the hollows left by the stones that were set in the building, the hollows we filled up?” And I said, “I forgot, sir.”

“Hear about them now,” he said. “These are the ones who have now heard my commandments and have repented with all their heart. And when the Lord saw that their repentance was good and pure, and that they could continue in it, he ordered their former sins to be blotted out. For these hollows were their sins, and they were made level, so that they would not show.”

finding.quote: Rather, consider that you have done a great work, if any of you suffers for God’s sake.
finding.source_quote: ἀλλὰ δοκεῖτε ἔργον μέγα πεποιηκέναι, ἐάν τις ὑμῶν διὰ τὸν θεὸν πάθῃ.
finding.why: Source's rhetorical question or rebuke ('do you think you have done a great work...?') is rendered as an imperative command, reversing the Shepherd's critique of pride into an instruction.
finding.fix: But do you think that you have done a great work, if any of you suffers for God’s sake?
finding.ruling: δοκεῖτε πεποιηκέναι expresses what they think, rebuked by οὐ νοεῖτε; imperative reverses rebuke into praise.

overrule.quote: Rather, consider that you have done a great work, if any of you suffers for God’s sake.
overrule.greek: ἀλλὰ δοκεῖτε ἔργον μέγα πεποιηκέναι, ἐάν τις ὑμῶν διὰ τὸν θεὸν πάθῃ.
overrule.checker_said: indicative rebuke: 'Yet you think you have done a great work'
overrule.why: δοκεῖτε is imperative or indicative by form; context decides. The sentence follows 'count yourselves blessed' and precedes 'the Lord is granting you life': encouragement to sufferers, not a rebuke.
